_meta.active: DURLOBACTAM SODIUM; DURLOBACTAM SODIUM; SULBACTAM SODIUM
_meta.indication: XACDURO is indicated in patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (HABP/VABP), caused by susceptible isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex.

pivotal_trials.design: Part A was the pivotal, randomized, assessor-blinded, comparative, noninferiority portion comparing IV SUL-DUR versus IV colistin, both with IV imipenem and cilastatin; randomization 1:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects ≥18 years of age with HABP, VABP, VP, or bacteremia caused by Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex (ABC).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: 28-day all-cause mortality in the CRABC m-MITT population.
pivotal_trials.n: 177 treated in Part A (randomized 181); 125 in the primary efficacy population (63 SUL-DUR, 62 colistin).
pivotal_trials.result: 28-day all-cause mortality was 19.0% (12/63) with SUL-DUR vs 32.3% (20/62) with colistin; treatment difference -13.2% (95% CI -30.0, 3.5), demonstrating noninferiority within the prespecified 20% margin.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were liver test abnormalities (19%), diarrhea (17%), anemia (13%), and hypokalemia (12%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 40% of XACDURO patients; treatment discontinuation due to any adverse reaction in 11% (10/91). Warnings: hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea.
target_moa: Co-packaged product of sulbactam, a beta-lactam antibacterial and Ambler Class A serine beta-lactamase inhibitor that is bactericidal by inhibiting ABC penicillin-binding proteins PBP1 and PBP3, plus durlobactam, a diazabicyclooctane non-beta-lactam beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects sulbactam from degradation by certain serine-beta-lactamases.
modality: Small molecule (co-packaged beta-lactam antibacterial/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination).

advisory_committee.vote: The Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee was convened April 17, 2023, and voted 12 "yes", 0 "no", 0 abstentions that the benefit-risk assessment is favorable for HABP/VABP caused by susceptible strains of ABC.

summary.text: SUL-DUR (XACDURO) was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA, received Priority Review, and was granted QIDP and Fast Track designations in 2017. It was a first cycle review, taken to the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (12-0 favorable), and received traditional approval based on a single phase 3 noninferiority trial meeting the 28-day all-cause mortality endpoint.
